text: According to a field note circulated Tuesday by the Maridun Antiquities Authority, the latest excavation at Tel Maridun was led by Dr. Yara Lindqvist, a Nordic University archaeologist whose team opened three trenches on the site’s eastern slope in late April. The note said the dig uncovered 14 sealed storage jars, a collapsed mudbrick wall and a small inscribed copper plaque dated provisionally to the 7th century BCE. Authority director Nabil Sorem confirmed the findings in a brief statement, adding that Dr. Lindqvist oversaw all trench work and artifact cataloguing. Funding came from the Aster Research Fund, and a preliminary report is expected by 18 November.
